adjudication_records.issue_text: current_user may be nil in TopicsController#unsubscribe (exempt from check_xhr, plain GET) causing NoMethodError on nil.id and a 500 for anonymous requests; missing requires_login-style guard (app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:101)

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the code calls `current_user.id` when doing `TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])`. The diff does not add any `requires_login`/authentication guard for this new GET action, and it is explicitly added to `skip_before_filter :check_xhr` and exposed via routes (`get ... => "topics#unsubscribe"`). If `current_user` is nil (anonymous request), this will raise `NoMethodError` on `.id`, causing a 500.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tu may be nil when the user has no TopicUser record, causing tu.notification_level to raise NoMethodError; should use find_or_create / TopicUser.change (app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:101-106)
tu.notification_level may be NULL for existing rows (codebase uses COALESCE elsewhere), so nil > TopicUser.notification_levels[:regular] raises (app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:104)

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the code does `if tu.notification_level > TopicUser.notification_levels[:regular]` after `tu = TopicUser.find_by(...)`. If an existing `topic_users` row has `notification_level` NULL (the diff itself shows other code paths using `COALESCE(topic_users.notification_level, :regular)` in `TopicUser.tracking`), then `tu.notification_level` will be `nil` and `nil > <integer>` will raise at runtime. This is a correctness issue in the newly added unsubscribe action.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unsubscribe performed via unauthenticated GET with no token: email prefetchers/bots can silently unsubscribe users, and it's a CSRF vector via cross-site requests

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a state-changing unsubscribe endpoint as a GET: `get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe" => "topics#unsubscribe"` (and the non-slug variant) in `config/routes.rb`, and `TopicsController#unsubscribe` mutates `TopicUser.notification_level` and `save!`s it. Because this is a GET with no per-user token or confirmation, it can be triggered by cross-site requests (e.g., ``) or by email client prefetchers, causing silent notification changes for any logged-in user with cookies. The controller also explicitly allows non-XHR (`skip_before_filter :check_xhr, only: [:show, :unsubscribe, :feed]`), making this easier to hit from non-app contexts.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Server route 't/:topic_id/unsubscribe' (no slug) is reachable and crashes rather than redirecting to the slugful URL; Ember route only handles the slugful path (app-route-map.js.es6:13)

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly adds a Rails route without a slug (`get "t/:topic_id/unsubscribe" => "topics#unsubscribe"`) but the `TopicsController#unsubscribe` action checks `(!request.format.json? && params[:slug].blank?)` and in that case returns a `301` redirect to `@topic_view.topic.unsubscribe_url` (which is built from `Topic#url`, i.e., the canonical slugful topic URL, plus `/unsubscribe`). That means the no-slug HTML path is intended to redirect rather than “crash”. While Ember only defines the slugful client route (`/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe`), the server-side redirect should prevent the app from booting on the no-slug URL in HTML mode. The claim of a crash is not demonstrated by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Explicit render :show added in perform_show_response's format.html may cause double-render behavior when the action is also invoked from #show (app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:497)

adjudication.rationale: In `perform_show_response`, the new `render :show` is inside the `respond_to` `format.html` block. When `#show` calls `perform_show_response`, this explicit render satisfies the response and prevents implicit rendering; it does not by itself create a second render. The diff does not show any additional `render` in `#show` that would combine with this to cause a double-render exception.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Full TopicView materialized in topics_controller.rb:98 just to toggle notification level — TopicView.new loads topic, posts, permissions, participants, but only TopicUser.find_by is needed, causing unbounded materialization proportional to topic size on every unsubscribe click (P2)

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the diff shows `@topic_view = TopicView.new(params[:topic_id], current_user)` followed by toggling `TopicUser` and then `perform_show_response`, which serializes/renders based on `@topic_view`. That means the unsubscribe endpoint builds a full TopicView even though the only state change here is `tu.notification_level`—an efficiency/architecture concern. However, the finding overstates that it’s done *only* to toggle notification level; the action also uses `@topic_view` for redirect logic (`@topic_view.topic.unsubscribe_url`) and to produce the response via `perform_show_response`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic-unsubscribe.js.es6:4-10 — PostStream.loadTopicView fetches the entire topic view JSON just to render a title and notification-level dropdown; topic model could be created with only needed fields (P3)

adjudication.rationale: In the new route `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6`, the `model(params)` hook creates a topic record and then calls `PostStream.loadTopicView(params.id)` and `topic.updateFromJson(json)`, which implies fetching the full topic-view JSON payload. The corresponding template (`templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs`) appears to only need `model.fancyTitle` (via `stopNotificiationsText`) and to render a notification-level control (`topic-notifications-button topic=model`). From the diff alone this is a plausible performance/architecture concern (over-fetching) rather than a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topics_controller.rb:95 — State-changing DB write on a GET route allows mail-client link prefetching/scanning (Outlook, SafeLinks, antivirus crawlers) to silently execute unsubscribes, muting users who never clicked (P1)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new `TopicsController#unsubscribe` action that updates `TopicUser.notification_level` and calls `tu.save!`, i.e., performs a state-changing DB write. The routes map this action to `GET` endpoints (`get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe" => "topics#unsubscribe"` and `get "t/:topic_id/unsubscribe" => "topics#unsubscribe"`), and `check_xhr` is explicitly skipped for `:unsubscribe`, making it callable as a normal GET. This creates a real risk that link prefetchers/scanners can trigger the unsubscribe/mute behavior without an intentional user action.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: GET request performs a destructive state change; email prefetchers/auto-scanners will silently unsubscribe users (unsubscribe mutates TopicUser.notification_level on a plain GET, violating HTTP safety semantics)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds GET routes `get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe" => "topics#unsubscribe"` and `get "t/:topic_id/unsubscribe" => "topics#unsubscribe"` (config/routes.rb). The `TopicsController#unsubscribe` action mutates persisted state by finding `TopicUser` and changing `tu.notification_level` then calling `tu.save!` (app/controllers/topics_controller.rb). Since this is triggered by a plain GET (and the email template now includes `%{unsubscribe_url}`), automated link prefetchers/scanners could trigger the destructive change without user intent, violating HTTP safety semantics.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: unsubscribe crashes with NoMethodError when no TopicUser record exists, since find_by can return nil and tu.notification_level then raises; should create the record at muted level instead

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the code does `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` and then immediately accesses `tu.notification_level` and assigns `tu.notification_level = ...` before `tu.save!`. If no `TopicUser` row exists for that user/topic, `find_by` returns `nil`, so `tu.notification_level` will raise `NoMethodError`. The diff does not include any guard or creation path for a missing record.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: unsubscribe_url is relative; Topic#url returns a path, so email links are broken; should be #{Discourse.base_url}#{url}/unsubscribe

adjudication.rationale: In this diff, `Topic#unsubscribe_url` is defined as `"#{url}/unsubscribe"` (app/models/topic.rb). Elsewhere in email templates they explicitly prefix `Discourse.base_url` to model URLs (e.g. `notification.html.erb` uses `<%= Discourse.base_url %><%= post.url %>`), which strongly indicates these `url`/`post.url` values are relative paths. The new email locale string `unsubscribe_link` (config/locales/server.en.yml) uses `%{unsubscribe_url}` directly in a markdown link, and the mailer passes `unsubscribe_url: post.topic.unsubscribe_url` (app/mailers/user_notifications.rb) without adding `Discourse.base_url`. If `Topic#url` is relative (as implied by existing email code), the unsubscribe link in emails will be relative and likely broken in many email clients; it should be absolute (e.g., `#{Discourse.base_url}#{url}/unsubscribe` or similar).

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: List-Unsubscribe header not updated to per-topic URL; it still points only to the old preferences URL while the new unsubscribe_url option only affects the body link

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `unsubscribe_url` being added to the email template args and used in the body via the `unsubscribe_link` I18n string (MessageBuilder `html_part` + server.en.yml). However, there is no code in this diff showing how the `List-Unsubscribe` header is constructed (e.g., in `Email::MessageBuilder#header_args`), so the claim that the header “still points only to the old preferences URL” is not verifiable from the provided changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: JSON-format unsubscribe responds via perform_show_response contract mismatch; the explicit render :show in the HTML branch changes rendering for all callers of perform_show_response, potentially altering topics#show HTML responses

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `render :show` only inside the `format.html` branch of `perform_show_response` (TopicsController), not the JSON branch. There is no evidence in the diff of a JSON response contract mismatch. The explicit `render :show` appears to be needed for the new `unsubscribe` action (which calls `perform_show_response`) so Rails renders the `show` template instead of looking for an `unsubscribe` template; for the existing `show` action, `render :show` is equivalent to the default rendering and does not change behavior. Any claim that this alters other callers cannot be verified from the diff (no other callers shown).

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: Frontend route requires slug while backend supports slug-less URL; Ember route only matches /t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe, failing to resolve slugless topic links

adjudication.rationale: While Ember only defines `topicUnsubscribe` at `/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe`, the Rails `TopicsController#unsubscribe` explicitly redirects slug-less HTML requests to the canonical slugged URL: `if slugs_do_not_match || (!request.format.json? && params[:slug].blank?) return redirect_to @topic_view.topic.unsubscribe_url`. Since `/t/:topic_id/unsubscribe` is an HTML entrypoint, it will 301 to `topic.unsubscribe_url` (built from `topic.url`, which is slugged) before the Ember app needs to match the route. Therefore the diff does not show a broken behavior where slug-less links fail to resolve.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: `TopicUser.find_by` can return nil when no TopicUser record exists, causing `tu.notification_level` to raise NoMethodError and a 500 on the unsubscribe flow; must handle nil case (default to tracking or create record) — app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:103

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the code assigns `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` and then immediately calls `tu.notification_level` and later `tu.save!` with no nil check. Since `find_by` can return `nil` when no `TopicUser` row exists for that user/topic, this would raise `NoMethodError` and break the unsubscribe flow with a 500 for that case.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: Unsubscribe action performs state mutation on a plain GET link embedded in email, so email scanners/prefetchers can silently unsubscribe users or unpredictably toggle state; should use POST/confirm page or signed one-time token — app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:98 / config/routes.rb

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds GET routes for `/t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe` and `/t/:topic_id/unsubscribe` (config/routes.rb) pointing to `TopicsController#unsubscribe`. That controller action mutates `TopicUser.notification_level` (toggling between `regular` and `muted`) and saves it (`tu.save!`) on every request, with no confirmation step and no signed/tokenized protection. The email template args now include `unsubscribe_url: post.topic.unsubscribe_url` and the server locale adds a clickable link to that URL, so an email client/scanner/prefetcher could trigger the GET and silently change state. This is a verifiable state-changing GET introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: `unsubscribe_link` locale string requires %{unsubscribe_url} but it's only substituted when add_unsubscribe_link option includes unsubscribe_url, so other MessageBuilder callers setting add_unsubscribe_link: true will hit I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument and fail email delivery — lib/email/message_builder.rb:70 / config/locales/server.en.yml:1852

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `unsubscribe_link` (server.en.yml) to include `%{unsubscribe_url}` unconditionally. In `Email::MessageBuilder#html_part`, when `@opts[:add_unsubscribe_link]` is true it calls `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` (lib/email/message_builder.rb) and `template_args` has no default `unsubscribe_url` key—it's only present if provided via opts. If any caller sets `add_unsubscribe_link: true` without also passing `unsubscribe_url`, this will raise `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument` and break email generation. The diff shows one caller updated to pass `unsubscribe_url`, but MessageBuilder itself is not made backward-compatible.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: `unsubscribe_url` in Topic returns a relative path (/t/slug/id), producing a broken link in emails unless prefixed with Discourse.base_url — app/models/topic.rb:719

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `Topic#unsubscribe_url` as `"#{url}/unsubscribe"` (app/models/topic.rb). This value is passed into email templates as `unsubscribe_url: post.topic.unsubscribe_url` (app/mailers/user_notifications.rb) and interpolated into the server locale markdown link without any `Discourse.base_url` prefix (config/locales/server.en.yml + lib/email/message_builder.rb). Since the diff itself does not show `Topic#url` being absolute and other email URLs explicitly prefix with `Discourse.base_url` (e.g., notification.html.erb uses `Discourse.base_url` + `post.url`), the new unsubscribe link is very likely relative and thus broken in emails.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: Using 301 (permanent) redirect for slug correction is semantically wrong and aggressively cached by browsers/CDNs; should use 302/307 — app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:100

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new `unsubscribe` action in `app/controllers/topics_controller.rb` that does `redirect_to @topic_view.topic.unsubscribe_url, status: 301` when `slugs_do_not_match || (!request.format.json? && params[:slug].blank?)`. The finding correctly points out the use of a 301 here and raises a concrete concern (permanent redirects being aggressively cached) tied to this new logic. However, from the diff alone it's not verifiable that 301 is definitively incorrect behavior (it may be intentional canonicalization), so this is a review concern rather than a provable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: Frontend topic-unsubscribe route has no .catch/error handling on PostStream.loadTopicView, leaving users with unhandled rejected promise and no feedback when topic is deleted, private, or request fails — app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6:5-9

adjudication.rationale: The newly added `topic-unsubscribe` route’s `model(params)` returns `PostStream.loadTopicView(params.id).then(...)` with no explicit error handling or `actions: { error(...) }` in the route. While Ember can route rejected model promises to an error substate, the diff does not show any route-level handling/UX for failures (e.g., topic not accessible), so the review concern is diff-grounded as an edge-case/UX completeness issue rather than a clearly verifiable broken behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: `tu.save!` raises on validation failure with no rescue (500), and bypasses TopicUser.change so the MessageBus notification is skipped and open topic pages won't reflect the change — app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:107

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the code mutates the `TopicUser` record directly (`tu.notification_level = ...; tu.save!`) rather than using `TopicUser.change(...)`. The diff shows `TopicUser.change` is responsible for publishing a MessageBus event when `notification_level` changes (`MessageBus.publish("/topic/#{topic_id}", { notification_level_change: ... }, ...)`). By bypassing it, any clients relying on that bus event (e.g., already-open topic pages) will not be notified of the change. The claim about `save!` raising on validation failure is plausible but not verifiable from the diff alone; however, the MessageBus bypass is directly evidenced.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: Toggle logic is inverted relative to unsubscribe semantics: a muted user clicking the 'stop notifications' link is re-enabled to regular, re-enabling notifications — app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:104-108

adjudication.rationale:
In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the logic is:

```rb
if tu.notification_level > TopicUser.notification_levels[:regular]
  tu.notification_level = TopicUser.notification_levels[:regular]
else
  tu.notification_level = TopicUser.notification_levels[:muted]
end
```

So a *muted* user (muted is not `> :regular`) will go through the `else` branch and remain/set to `:muted`, not be re-enabled to `:regular`. The finding’s specific claim (“a muted user ... is re-enabled to regular”) is not supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No test coverage for the new TopicsController#unsubscribe action; toggle logic, slug-mismatch redirect, and show rendering are all untested

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new `TopicsController#unsubscribe` action with nontrivial behavior (slug-mismatch redirect, toggling `TopicUser.notification_level` between `:regular` and `:muted`, and calling `perform_show_response`/HTML `render :show`). The only test change shown is in `spec/components/email/message_builder_spec.rb` for `unsubscribe_url`, and there is no new or updated spec covering the controller action’s redirect or toggle logic. So the finding is specific and grounded: this new action is untested in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Missing edge case: TopicUser.find_by may return nil for users who never visited the topic, causing NoMethodError on tu.notification_level and a 500 error

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the code does `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` and then immediately calls `tu.notification_level` without checking `tu` for nil. The diff shows no guarantee that a `TopicUser` row exists for every user/topic pair, so `find_by` can return nil and cause a `NoMethodError` (500) on `tu.notification_level`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unauthenticated state-changing GET unsubscribe route will be triggered by email link prefetching (mail clients/scanners), muting users without intent; no idempotency/confirmation guard or test

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a state-changing GET endpoint `topics#unsubscribe` (`get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe" => "topics#unsubscribe"` and `get "t/:topic_id/unsubscribe" ...`) that mutates `TopicUser.notification_level` and `save!`s it, toggling between `:regular` and `:muted` (or lowering higher levels to `:regular`). The email template args now include `unsubscribe_url: post.topic.unsubscribe_url`, and the server-side `unsubscribe_link` text includes a direct link to that URL. Because this mutation is triggered by a plain GET (no confirmation, no POST/CSRF semantics, no idempotent “set to X” behavior), automated link prefetching/scanning by mail clients can inadvertently change a user’s notification state. The diff also doesn’t add tests covering this new behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: New message-builder test only asserts List-Unsubscribe header presence with a hard-coded fake relative unsubscribe_url, not matching production absolute URL, and doesn't assert the unsubscribe link renders in text/html

adjudication.rationale: The spec change adds `unsubscribe_url: "/t/1234/unsubscribe"` and (per the finding) only asserts the `List-Unsubscribe` header is present, without asserting `%{unsubscribe_link}` is actually substituted into the rendered HTML/text. That’s a concrete test-coverage gap for the new `unsubscribe_url` plumbing (`user_notifications.rb` passes `unsubscribe_url`, `server.en.yml` uses it, `message_builder.rb` gsubs `%{unsubscribe_link}`). However, the claim that production uses an absolute URL isn’t verifiable from the diff: `Topic#unsubscribe_url` is built from `url`, and nothing here shows it being absolute vs relative.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No integration test covering the email → unsubscribe flow chain (unsubscribe_url passing, %{unsubscribe_link} interpolation, template rendering)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new per-topic unsubscribe flow into notification emails: `UserNotifications#send_notification_email` now passes `unsubscribe_url: post.topic.unsubscribe_url` (app/mailers/user_notifications.rb), the server locale `unsubscribe_link` template now includes `%{unsubscribe_url}` (config/locales/server.en.yml), and `Email::MessageBuilder#html_part` interpolates `%{unsubscribe_link}` into the HTML override (lib/email/message_builder.rb). The only test change is in `message_builder_spec.rb`, adding `unsubscribe_url` to the builder opts, but it still only asserts the `List-Unsubscribe` header and does not exercise the end-to-end rendering/interpolation of `%{unsubscribe_link}` or the full mailer → builder → template chain. So the finding about missing integration/e2e coverage for this new flow is supported by the diff and is a substantive test gap rather than a direct runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: perform_show_response behavior change (explicit render :show with check_xhr skipped) is untested for the unsubscribe path

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new `TopicsController#unsubscribe` action, skips `check_xhr` for it (`skip_before_filter :check_xhr, only: [:show, :unsubscribe, :feed]`), and then calls `perform_show_response`. In `perform_show_response`, the HTML branch now explicitly does `render :show` after preloading (`format.html do ... store_preloaded(...); render :show end`). This changes how the unsubscribe HTML request is served (and also affects any caller of `perform_show_response`), but the only added spec is for `Email::MessageBuilder` and nothing in the diff adds coverage for the unsubscribe controller/route behavior or the HTML rendering path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: Crash in unsubscribe when no TopicUser record exists — find_by returns nil and tu.notification_level raises NoMethodError (topics_controller.rb:103)

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the diff adds `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` and then immediately reads/writes `tu.notification_level` and calls `tu.save!` with no nil-check. If no `TopicUser` row exists for that user/topic, `find_by` returns `nil` and `tu.notification_level` will raise `NoMethodError`. This is directly evident from the added code path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: Missing unsubscribe_url interpolation for other email senders — only send_notification_email passes it, other Email::MessageBuilder consumers will hit I18n missing-interpolation or broken links

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `config/locales/server.en.yml` `unsubscribe_link` to interpolate `%{unsubscribe_url}`. `Email::MessageBuilder#html_part` always renders this via `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` whenever `@opts[:add_unsubscribe_link]` is true, but `MessageBuilder` does not provide a default `unsubscribe_url` in `@template_args` (it only merges `@opts`). Only one caller in the diff (`UserNotifications#send_notification_email`) was updated to pass `unsubscribe_url`, and the spec was adjusted similarly. Any other existing `Email::MessageBuilder` usage setting `add_unsubscribe_link: true` without `unsubscribe_url` would raise missing interpolation or produce a broken link.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: CSRF vulnerability — state-changing unsubscribe action performed on GET without CSRF token or nonce, allowing third-party pages to silently modify notification settings

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a state-changing `TopicsController#unsubscribe` action that toggles and saves `TopicUser.notification_level` (`tu.notification_level = ...; tu.save!`) but exposes it via `get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe" => "topics#unsubscribe"` and `get "t/:topic_id/unsubscribe" => "topics#unsubscribe"`. Because it is a GET endpoint and there is no CSRF token/nonce check shown (and Rails’ CSRF protection typically does not apply to GET), a third-party page could trigger this URL in a logged-in user’s browser and silently change notification settings.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: Anonymous access raises — current_user.id called without signed-in check causes NoMethodError on nil instead of login redirect; also renders topic content to anonymous users

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the code assumes a logged-in user and an existing `TopicUser` row: `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` then immediately calls `tu.notification_level` and mutates/saves it. From the diff alone, there is no guard ensuring `current_user` is present (or non-anonymous) and no handling for `tu == nil` (e.g., user never had a TopicUser record). Either case leads to `NoMethodError` (`nil.id` or `nil.notification_level`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: Unsubscribe toggles rather than unsubscribes — a :regular user gets fully muted and a muted user is flipped back to regular, contradicting the link's promise

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the logic does not toggle a muted user back to regular. It sets `notification_level` to `:regular` only when the current level is greater than `:regular` (e.g., tracking/watching), otherwise it sets it to `:muted`. So a `:regular` user becomes muted, and a `:muted` user remains muted; there is no flip from muted to regular shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: Typo in controller property name stopNotificiationsText ('Notificiations') in topic-unsubscribe.js.es6
matched_golden_ids: Typo in property name: 'stopNotificiationsText' should be 'stopNotificationsText' (missing 'n' in 'Notifications')
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags the same misspelled property name `stopNotificiationsText` ("Notificiations") that the golden comment identifies, implying it should be corrected to `stopNotificationsText`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: Duplicate respond_instructions footer — %{respond_instructions} rendered twice in notification.html.erb, now adjacent to %{unsubscribe_link}

adjudication.rationale:
In `app/views/email/notification.html.erb`, `%{respond_instructions}` appears twice in the rendered HTML when `context_posts.present?`: once inside the `if context_posts.present?` block (`
%{respond_instructions}
`) and again unconditionally near the bottom right before `%{unsubscribe_link}`. `Email::MessageBuilder#html_part` uses `gsub!` on `%{respond_instructions}`, so both placeholders will be replaced, resulting in duplicated instructions in the outgoing email.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: Front-end route mangles slugs / inconsistent with server routes — client requires slug+id while server allows slug-less /t/1234/unsubscribe links

adjudication.rationale: The client route is defined as `/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe` (app-route-map.js.es6) while the server defines both slugged and slug-less routes. However, the server `TopicsController#unsubscribe` explicitly redirects HTML requests with a blank slug to `@topic_view.topic.unsubscribe_url` (301), which is a slugged URL (`Topic#unsubscribe_url` appends `/unsubscribe` to `Topic#url`, which in Discourse is typically `/t/:slug/:id`). So the slug-less server route is an intentional compatibility entry point that redirects to the slugged URL the client route expects, rather than a broken inconsistency shown by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `topics_controller.rb` ~line 101: `tu.notification_level` called unconditionally on result of `TopicUser.find_by`, causing NoMethodError on nil (500) for users with no topic_users row; needs `TopicUser.get` or nil guard/create

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` can return `nil`, but the code immediately calls `tu.notification_level` and later `tu.save!` without any guard or creation path. This will raise `NoMethodError` for users who don't yet have a `topic_users` row for that topic, resulting in a 500.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `topics_controller.rb`: `unsubscribe` action lacks `requires_login` and skips `check_xhr`, so anonymous requests hit `current_user.id` on nil → 500; also `TopicView.new(params[:topic_id], current_user)` with nil user leaks topic visibility and renders the topic page to anonymous users

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the new action immediately does `TopicView.new(params[:topic_id], current_user)` and then `TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, ...)`. The diff also adds `:unsubscribe` to `skip_before_filter :check_xhr`, and there is no diff-shown `requires_login`/nil-guard around `current_user`. If an anonymous request hits this route, `current_user` can be nil and `current_user.id` will raise (500). The action also calls `perform_show_response` (HTML renders `:show`), so without an authentication/authorization gate in this method, it risks serving topic content to unauthenticated users.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unsubscribe is a state-changing GET with no CSRF token, vulnerable to prefetchers/crawlers silently muting users or attackers force-toggling a victim's notification state; should be POST with a token or require login + confirmation

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new GET route (`get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe" => "topics#unsubscribe"` and `get "t/:topic_id/unsubscribe"`) that maps to `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, which *modifies persisted state* by toggling `TopicUser.notification_level` and calling `tu.save!`. Because this is a state-changing action over GET, it is vulnerable to unintended triggering (e.g., link prefetchers/crawlers) and CSRF-style forced navigation (an attacker can cause a logged-in victim’s browser to request the URL). The diff does not show any CSRF token requirement or confirmation step for this action; Rails CSRF protections typically target non-GET methods, so this design is a verifiable security defect from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `server.en.yml`/`message_builder.rb`: `%{unsubscribe_url}` is only injected in `send_notification_email`, so other mail paths using `add_unsubscribe_link` get an empty href ('' → links to current page), producing a broken unsubscribe link; the message_builder_spec change only re-tests header presence and never exercises the interpolation

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `config/locales/server.en.yml`’s `unsubscribe_link` to interpolate `%{unsubscribe_url}`. In `lib/email/message_builder.rb`, that string is rendered whenever `add_unsubscribe_link` is true, and `template_args` only includes keys explicitly merged from `@opts`. The diff shows `unsubscribe_url` being added only in `UserNotifications#send_notification_email` (and the spec now passes `unsubscribe_url` too), so any other caller that sets `add_unsubscribe_link: true` but does not provide `unsubscribe_url` would now have a missing interpolation value (likely raising or producing a bad link). The claim about “other mail paths” and the exact “empty href” outcome isn’t directly verifiable from the diff, but the risk/incompleteness created by requiring a new interpolation key is grounded in the changes shown, and the spec indeed doesn’t assert the interpolation/link content.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `topics_controller.rb`: `slugs_do_not_match` reads `params[:slug]` which is nil on the `t/:topic_id/unsubscribe` route, always triggering a 301 redirect; the slugless route never serves content, crawlers get an extra redirect, and the permanent 301 bakes in stale slugs after renames; `params[:topic_id]` string vs `show` inconsistency

adjudication.rationale: In the new `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the guard `if slugs_do_not_match || (!request.format.json? && params[:slug].blank?)` will be true for the slugless route `get "t/:topic_id/unsubscribe"` (since `params[:slug]` is nil/blank), causing an unconditional `301` redirect to `@topic_view.topic.unsubscribe_url`. This makes the slugless route effectively a redirect-only endpoint (potentially redundant) and introduces an extra permanent redirect hop for `/t/:topic_id/unsubscribe` requests. The finding’s broader claims about `slugs_do_not_match` internals and `topic_id` string inconsistency can’t be verified from the diff, but the redirect behavior itself is directly evidenced.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `unsubscribe.hbs`: `{{{stopNotificiationsText}}}` renders user-influenced content raw, bypassing Ember XSS escaping — an XSS vector if any plugin/translation path doesn't pre-encode; also the computed name is misspelled (`stopNotificiationsText`)

adjudication.rationale: In `templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs` the new `{{{stopNotificiationsText}}}` uses triple-stash (unescaped) rendering. The controller computes this string via `I18n.t("topic.unsubscribe.stop_notifications", { title: this.get("model.fancyTitle") })`, and the translation includes raw HTML (`{{title}}`). Since `model.fancyTitle` is derived from the topic title (user-influenced content) and the template explicitly bypasses Ember escaping, this introduces a credible XSS risk in the diff if the interpolation path doesn’t guarantee escaping. The misspelling exists (`stopNotificiationsText`) but is consistently used in controller+template so it’s not itself a functional break; the unescaped render is the defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `routes.rb`: summary routes lost the `post_number: /\d+/` constraint in an unrelated drive-by change, allowing arbitrary strings into `#show` params

adjudication.rationale: In `config/routes.rb`, both summary routes previously included `constraints: { topic_id: /\d+/, post_number: /\d+/ }` but now only constrain `topic_id` (`post_number` constraint was removed). This is a behavior change that weakens parameter validation and can allow non-numeric `post_number` values to reach `topics#show` where they were previously rejected by routing constraints.
